title: PersonaSceneBundle
description: Output contract for 100x-persona. Self-contained in this skill (this repo has no shared cross-skill schemas/ yet). One script draft in -> who-delivers-it (personas) + where-it's-set (scenes) + how-they-pair-to-script-spans (pairings) out. CORE DESIGN: scenes is a TOP-LEVEL sibling map to personas, not a string field nested inside a persona object -- this enforces the independent scene entity design. NOTE (structural limits of vanilla JSON Schema draft-07, same class of gap as 100x-search-query's schema.json): this file can enforce PER-ITEM shape (required fields, non-vague-word pattern on scene location fields, ID-format patterns on persona_ref/scene_ref) but CANNOT enforce CROSS-OBJECT referential integrity -- e.g. a pairing.persona_ref of 'PERSONA_GHOST' that matches the ^PERSONA_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ pattern but does not exist as an actual key in the personas map passes this schema cleanly. Same limitation applies to: (a) evidence-quote-must-be-a-literal-substring-of-source_script checks (cross-field, not expressible in JSON Schema at all), and (b) orphan detection (every defined persona/scene key must be referenced by >=1 pairing). All three are enforced by the real, runnable scripts/validate.js, which loads this file at runtime and reuses its ID patterns and vague-word pattern so the two files can't silently drift. See axioms.md for the split.

source_script.description: The exact script/copy text this bundle was derived from, verbatim. This is the ground truth every *_evidence_quote / *_pain_quote / script_span_quote is checked against (literal substring, case-sensitive) by scripts/validate.js. Must not contain real customer/brand identifiers when used in this repo's evals/ (synthetic only).

personas.description: Map of persona_id -> persona. Independent top-level entity map, keyed by ID. A persona describes WHO delivers the script (identity/authority + who they're speaking to), never a scene.

scenes.description: Map of scene_id -> scene. Independent top-level entity map, keyed by ID, sibling of `personas` (NOT nested inside any persona object). A scene describes WHERE/WHEN a script span is set -- it has its own identity and can in principle be reused across personas/pairings; it is never serialized as a bare string field on a persona.

pairings.description: The join table: which persona delivers which scene at which script span. This is the only place personas and scenes are connected to each other and to the script.

warnings.description: Non-fatal flags, e.g. 'audience_pain_quote inferred from weak signal, low confidence' (workflow.md Phase 1 soft-degrade rule).

identity_label.description: Short label for who is speaking (e.g. '十一年经验夜班ICU护士'). Generic descriptor, never a real person's name or a customer category dictionary entry.

authority_basis.description: One line explaining why this narrator is credible/relatable to say this (credential-based OR peer-relatability-based -- see axioms.md #2, script text is not required to contain a formal credential).

authority_evidence_quote.description: Literal quote from source_script anchoring authority_basis. Must be an exact substring of source_script (axiom 2, checked by scripts/validate.js, not expressible in schema.json alone).

audience_fit.description: Who this persona is speaking to, in generic/category terms (never a customer-specific audience dictionary entry).

audience_pain_quote.description: Literal quote from source_script anchoring audience_fit. Must be an exact substring of source_script (axiom 2, checked by scripts/validate.js).

delivery_style.description: One line on tone/register (e.g. '第一人称经历叙述，平实口语').

relationship_to_camera.description: Generic taxonomy of narrator-to-viewer address mode, not a customer-specific enum.

appearance_note.description: Optional. One-line wardrobe/visual descriptor. Not a generation prompt -- that belongs to a downstream prompt-composition skill.

scene_name.description: Short label for this scene, e.g. '卧室房门早间训练'.

trigger_moment.pattern: ^(?!.*(某处|随便|某个地方|某场景|某个场景|某个地点|某地|某时|待定|TBD|tbd|somewhere|Somewhere|anywhere|Anywhere)).+$
trigger_moment.description: When in the viewer's day/life this scene naturally occurs (axiom 3, P.A.I.N.S.-style 'Scene' dimension: actual moment, not an imagined generic one). Vague-word pattern blocks placeholder answers; see axioms.md #3 for the full list.

location.pattern: ^(?!.*(某处|随便|某个地方|某场景|某个场景|某个地点|某地|某时|待定|TBD|tbd|somewhere|Somewhere|anywhere|Anywhere)).+$

micro_coordinate.pattern: ^(?!.*(某处|随便|某个地方|某场景|某个场景|某个地点|某地|某时|待定|TBD|tbd|somewhere|Somewhere|anywhere|Anywhere)).+$
micro_coordinate.description: Specific positioning/framing within the location (e.g. '弹力带绕在卧室门把手上'), not just the location name repeated (axiom 3).

visual_props.description: At least 2 concrete, visible objects in frame. Generic categories only -- never a specific real brand/product name.

segment_ref.description: Optional. If an upstream 100x-segment segment id is available, echo it here. Absence never blocks this skill (class-C silent-skip, see workflow.md Phase 1).

script_span_quote.description: Literal quote from source_script anchoring which span of the script this persona+scene pairing applies to. Must be an exact substring of source_script (checked by scripts/validate.js).

persona_ref.description: Must reference a key that exists in the top-level `personas` map. Schema.json can only check the ID FORMAT, not that the key actually exists -- that referential-integrity check is scripts/validate.js's job (axiom 1).

scene_ref.description: Must reference a key that exists in the top-level `scenes` map. Same schema-vs-script split as persona_ref (axiom 1).

rationale.description: One line on why this persona+scene combination fits this script span.
